extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and prospective authors/contributors to Notices of the American Mathematical Society (including mathematics educators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and editorial standards for writing and submitting pieces (expository mathematics, education, opinion, and professional items) to the Notices of the American Mathematical Society, including expectations about audience, level, labeling of opinions, and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sizable target audience / colloquium-in-writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of mathematics articles are urged to think in terms of giving a kind of colloquium in written form and to keep in mind some particular 'sizable target audience' while writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rarely can such an audience consist entirely of experts; successful articles are bounded above in level—approximately the level of the more widely appreciated AMS invited hour addresses. Aim to interest a large number of readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository article content and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Expository articles should include some history and provide a context for appreciating the mathematics; they should lead to the frontier and illuminate interconnections between different areas of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write so that a sizable target audience can follow and appreciate the subject; the article should both inform broadly and point readers toward current research directions and connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education articles: viewpoint, quality, and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Education articles reflecting mathematicians' viewpoints from pre-school through graduate school are welcome; they should be well written and well informed and should enlighten a sizable number of readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notices seeks to promote discussion among mathematicians and mathematics educators and to inform readers about mathematics education. To prevent acrimonious debate, negative comments should not be directed toward personalities, specific programs, or whole fields of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional items: appropriate topics to report
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices reports about many things concerning the mathematics profession, including the job market, faculty salaries, grant support for research, conditions for graduate students, notable achievements, backlogs in journals, and related items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such reporting should be informative to the Notices' broad readership; for example, the Notices will undertake in-depth studies such as the cost of publishing from multiple viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinion labeling and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal opinions must be clearly delineated from official AMS positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorials will be statements about the Notices or elaborations of AMS policies written by the Editorial Board or certain officials. Pieces representing largely individual opinions should appear in the 'In My Opinion' column, as letters to the editor, or in special pieces clearly marked as opinion items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship attribution / signed pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Essentially everything other than advertising, certain lists, and information about meetings is signed by the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain transparent authorship by signing submissions so readers know the source of viewpoints and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedures and format preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters to the Editor, Forum pieces, articles, and reviews may be sent to the editor by e-mail, fax, or postal mail; electronic submissions are preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide contact addresses (email, fax, postal) and follow the Notices' stated submission channels; correspondence with the managing editor may be sent to the given email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising policy and allowable advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices publishes situations-wanted and classified advertising, and display advertising for publishers and academic or scientific organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising content is limited to these categories; editorial content (other than specified exceptions) is signed and separate from advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding acrimony in educational debate
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent acrimonious debate—which inhibits serious discussion—negative comments should not be directed toward personalities, specific programs, or whole fields of inquiry in education pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame critiques and discussions constructively and focus on issues and evidence rather than personal or institutional attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of impact relative to invited addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: An article in the Notices has impact on more people and more mathematics than an invited address does; the Notices aspires to attract authors with the same eagerness as for AMS invited hour addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful realization of the Notices' goals would be when potential authors are as eager to accept an invitation to write for the Notices as to accept an invitation to give an AMS hour address; strive for accessibility and broad appeal.
